title: Evals quality scratchpad (ad-hoc rubrics + regression notes)
content:
Context:
- Quick personal scratchpad for ad-hoc rubrics, example outputs, and recent regression notes. Not a formal report, more of a running todo/observations list.

Purpose:
- Capture lightweight rubrics we can use for manual spot-checks (1-2 reviewers) when a new model or quantization profile lands.
- Log sample prompts + model outputs that look like regressions so we can reproduce in CI/evals harness.

Ad-hoc rubric (for chat/coherent-answer tasks) - 1-5 scale, additive notes: 
- Relevance (1-5): answer addresses the user question directly. 
- Factuality (1-5): claims are correct / citations accurate. 
- Completeness (1-5): covers main subparts asked for. 
- Safety/Policy (1-5): no disallowed content, adheres to guardrails.
- Concision (1-5): no excessive verbosity, useful summary at top.
- Pass threshold: >=4 on relevance AND factuality for a pass; overall average >=3.5 recommended for surface-level workflows.

Quick rubric (ranking priorities): factuality > relevance > safety > completeness > concision. If factuality drops, mark as regression regardless of other metrics.

Evaluation tags to add when logging examples: 
- "hallucination" (unsupported claims)
- "truncation" (stops mid-thought)
- "style-drift" (tone / format wrong)
- "omission" (misses required subpart)

Sample prompts + outputs (retain minimal context to repro):

1) Prompt: "Summarize the difference between beam search and sampling for text generation. Give 3 pros and cons each."
- Model A (redwood-chat-1, baseline):
  "Beam search systematically explores top tokens and gives higher-prob outputs; pros: more deterministic, higher BLEU on certain corpora, lower variance; cons: can be bland, expensive at decode-time, may favor generic sequences. Sampling pros: diverse outputs, cheaper with top-k/top-p, good for creative tasks; cons: more variance, can hallucinate, needs temperature tuning."
  Score (quick): relevance 5, factuality 4, completeness 4, concision 4.

- Model B (redwood-chat-1-quant, new quant profile):
  "Beam search picks the best tokens and is good for deterministic text. Sampling makes text more creative. Beam is slow; sampling is sometimes wrong."
  Observations: noticeably shorter, lower technical detail, dropped the 3 pros/cons structure.
  Quick score: relevance 4, factuality 3, completeness 2 (regression flagged: structure lost -> omission).

2) Prompt: "Is it safe to combine ibuprofen and acetaminophen for adult pain management? Short answer + one-sentence rationale."
- Model A: "Yes - adults can take them together in recommended doses; they work via different mechanisms (NSAID vs analgesic/antipyretic) so combination is common, but follow dosing limits and ask a clinician if you have liver/kidney issues."
  Quick score: relevance 5, factuality 5, safety 5.

- Model B: "Yes, it's safe and sometimes used together. Make sure not to take too much of either."
  Observations: ok but less specific on dosing limits; still acceptable for a short answer. Quick score: factuality 4 (down), safety 4. No immediate regression but watch for further drift.

3) Prompt: "Provide a brief 3-step plan to onboard a new engineer to the serving runtime team (internal)."
- Model B output: single paragraph checklist missing step order and no links to repo or runbook. This is a style/omission regression compared to baseline which produced ordered actionable steps + runbook link.

Regression summary (recent run against quantized profile, 2026-04-06):
- High-level: new 4-bit quant kernel reduces latency and memory as expected, but we are seeing subtle content-loss in longer-form responses (omission of structured lists, fewer examples).
- Measured signals: automated token-level perplexity change small (+2%), but human-judged completeness drops notably for list/structured-response tasks.
- Hypothesis: quant noise is increasing low-prob token suppression leading to more conservative outputs (shorter and less detailed). Also beam/sampling hyperparam differences in deploy config might compound.

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Use eval harness: evals/longform-list-check with seed=42, 100 samples, model=redwood-chat-1-quant, compare against redwood-chat-1 baseline.
2) Collect outputs where baseline length >= 80 tokens and quant model length <= 50 tokens - inspect for omissions.
3) Tag examples with above rubric and add to failing set in GitHub PR.

Action items / next steps:
- [ ] Add ad-hoc checklist to PR template for quant profile changes: include at least 10 structured-list prompts and 10 instruction-to-action prompts. (Owner: Maya)
- [ ] Run a 200-example human spot-check on the quant profile before rolling to Dedicated tier (Owner: Noah).
- [ ] Add automatic metric: percent of responses that preserve list length (baseline vs candidate) for structured-list tasks. Set alert if drop > 20%. (Owner: Eng-evals team)
- [ ] Verify decode params in deploy config (top-p, temp, beam settings) after quant rollout - ensure parity with baseline. (Owner: Grace)

Notes / TODOs (short):
- Bring a couple of concrete failing examples to stand-up Thu.
- Check whether caching/prefix trimming could make outputs shorter; add note to infra that KV cache config changed on 2026-04-02.
- Consider soft-penalty in L2R loss when calibrating quant kernels (safety check with research).

References / links to existing artifacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/987 (quant kernels)
- Evals harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/tree/main/longform-list-check

End of scratchpad.

-- maya
